propositions: add_comment returns raw ACLI batch envelope ({"results": [...], "successCount": N}) instead of normalized comment resource, allowing results[].id (a work item key) to be mistaken for a comment id
the declared return type and consumer expectation (dict with "id" field as comment resource) does not match the actual batch envelope structure returned
existing sibling methods (get_comments, get_issue, create_issue) normalize their payloads at the transport boundary while add_comment skips this pattern

a normalizer function _parse_comment_created must wrap json.loads to distinguish between DC/REST comment resources (pass through verbatim), Cloud batch envelopes (normalize to {"id": None, "acli_envelope": ...}), and invalid shapes (raise RuntimeError)
the remaining --json mutation wrappers in acli_cli_ops and module-level acli.update_issue must be audited for the same raw-passthrough hazard
